Test for differential spatial patterns using MiSA

Source: R/MiSA_test.R
MiSA.Rd

Performs hypothesis testing to detect differential spatial patterns between two groups, for each taxon in MiSA_data, using one of four available MiSA tests.

Usage

MiSA(misa_data_list, method = "area", omnibus_r = NULL, omnibus_num = NULL)

Arguments

misa_data_list

A named list, with one element per taxon, as returned by MiSA_data and MiSA_check. Each element must contain group, a vector of group labels, and d, a matrix of estimated \(d\)-curves.

method

Character string specifying which test to perform. One of "orig", "abs", "sup", or "area". Defaults to "area".

omnibus_r

Optional numeric vector specifying the specific radii at which to evaluate the test statistic, used only when method = "orig" or method = "abs". Defaults to NULL.

omnibus_num

Optional integer specifying the number of radii, evenly spaced across the available range, at which to evaluate the test statistic, used only when method = "orig" or method = "abs" and omnibus_r is not specified. Defaults to NULL.

Value

A list containing taxon-specific p-values and a community-level p-value assessing overall spatial dysbiosis. For method = "area" or method = "sup", taxon-specific effect sizes are additionally returned. For method = "orig" or method = "abs", a per_r_pval element is additionally returned, describing the testing results at each of the specified radii.

Details

Four tests are available via the method argument:

"orig"

Evaluates the raw statistic \(d(r)\) (capturing both the magnitude and direction of deviation from CSR) at a set of pre-selected radii, and combines the resulting p-values across radii using the harmonic mean p-value (HMP) method.

"abs"

Similar to "orig", but compares the absolute value of \(d(r)\) (capturing only the magnitude of deviation) at the selected radii instead.

"sup"

Evaluates the maximum absolute deviation, \(\max_r |d(r)|\), capturing signals that may arise at any spatial scale.

"area"

Evaluates the integrated magnitude of deviation of \(d(r)\) across the full range of radii, capturing signals that may arise at any spatial scale.

For "orig" and "abs", the radii used can be specified via omnibus_r or omnibus_num. If omnibus_r is specified, the function always uses omnibus_r, regardless of the input for omnibus_num. If omnibus_r is left at its default (NULL) and omnibus_num is specified, the function uses omnibus_num evenly spaced radii instead. If both omnibus_r and omnibus_num are left at their defaults (NULL), the function sets omnibus_num = min(5, c - 1), where c is the number of radii available for that taxon.

This function uses whichever group is entered as groupA (during data preparation) as the reference group. A negative effect size indicates that the summary statistic is smaller in the reference group than in the comparison group, indicating that the comparison group is more spatially structured (e.g., exhibiting stronger clustering or regularity) relative to the reference group.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- MiSA(misa_data_list = data_checked, method = "area")
result <- MiSA(misa_data_list = data_checked, method = "orig", omnibus_r = c(300, 600, 900))
result <- MiSA(misa_data_list = data_checked, method = "abs", omnibus_num = 6)
} # }
